title: SIU called in after man shot dead by police
article: The fatal shooting of a 49-year-old man Wednesday is being probed by the province's Special Investigations Unit.
The man was shot after 9:30 p.m. at a rooming house on Spadina Rd., south of the TTC Dupont subway station.

"(Toronto) police were notified of a man with a knife in the area of 140 Spadina Rd. Officers attended the area. A short time later, there was an interaction between the officers and a man and he was shot," the SIU said Thursday.
The man was pronounced dead at St. Michael's Hospital.
A second man in his 60s was taken to hospital with stab wounds to his torso and was listed in serious condition.
SIU spokesman Monica Hudon said they aren't looking into the stabbed man's case because his injuries weren't caused by police.
A tenant who lives on the first floor of the rooming house says the man was shot in the front of the rooming house's driveway, close to the street.
He said he doesn't know what led to the altercation between the two men who both lived at the rooming house.
"They lived side-by-side on the third floor. One was retired and the other did whatever he did," said the tenant who didn't want to be named.
He said he and four other tenants at the rooming house were kept in a TTC bus while the police investigated.
As of Thursday morning, there was still quite a bit of blood spattered on the rooming house property and sidewalk, which police say is the responsibility of the house owner to clean.
Police don't comment on a case once the SIU is involved.
